title: 5/28, Ray Co Commissioners Mtg
showNotes:
# County Commission Meeting Summary

## Meeting Overview
The county commission meeting was called to order, beginning with the Pledge of Allegiance and confirmation that both audio and video recording were in progress. The commission approved minutes from a previous meeting with minor punctuation corrections.

## State Auditor's Report Discussion
A citizen named Kurt Croy raised concerns regarding a follow-up report from the state auditor, which noted that 17 of 18 closed meetings may have discussed topics outside the scope permitted for closed sessions under Sunshine Law requirements. Croy questioned whether the commission planned to release minutes from those meetings and clarify what changes were being implemented.

Commissioners responded that they had a productive meeting with the auditor and acknowledged the difficulty of staying strictly on topic during closed sessions, noting that residual issues sometimes arise during discussions. Commissioners explained that, unlike larger counties that have attorneys present during meetings to provide immediate guidance, their commission lacks that level of legal oversight. The commission stated they are making efforts to follow the auditor's recommendations and remain focused on topics covered under statute. However, commissioners noted they had not yet reviewed the full written report and would address it further after doing so.

## Janitorial Services Contract Approved
The commission reviewed and approved a janitorial services bid from Mike Kenney. The bid had been previously reviewed, with commissioners suggesting approximately five additions to the proposal, including bonding requirements. A motion to accept the bid was made, seconded, and approved unanimously.

## Old Jail Property Discussion
Commissioners discussed the ongoing challenge of the old jail property, including annual insurance costs of approximately $4,300. The commission expressed interest in determining the building's actual value and the costs associated with keeping it, including potential demolition expenses described as "exorbitant." A realtor was reportedly contacted to assess the property, and commissioners were to follow up with her that week. The discussion highlighted the difficulty in finding a solution for the property, with no clear consensus on whether to sell, renovate, or demolish the building.

## Emergency Operations Center Internet Service
The commission reviewed a contract for internet service at the Emergency Operations Center (EOC). During discussion, it was noted that the county currently pays approximately $87 monthly for local internet service through Carl Harper's office. Commissioners agreed to cancel that existing service once the new arrangement is established. Documentation regarding the monthly service costs was requested for review.

## Detention Officer Training Platform
A contract was presented for a training platform for detention officers, following NITO accreditation standards. The training system provides a structured program for staff from day one, including testing and a path to certification. This initiative is part of efforts toward accreditation, which could potentially help reduce liability for the sheriff's office. All detention staff will be required to complete the training.

## Jail Management System Change
A significant discussion occurred regarding a change in jail management software. The commission had previously contracted with Omnigo for a new jail management system, but implementation experienced multiple delays and complications. Issues included poor communication between departments, delayed customization of reports, and questions about proper licensing.

The sheriff's representative met with an owner of Cadence Software at a jail conference and was impressed with the product. Cadence is described as more intuitive because it was developed from a jail administrator's perspective. Clinton County Sheriff's Office and other agencies using the software provided positive feedback.

Key points about the change:
- The new Cadence system is cheaper than the previous arrangement
- Implementation deadline is targeted for June 1st
- Integrations with other software are included rather than charged separately
- The system was demonstrated to be intuitive enough that staff could book an inmate from start to finish without instructions
- The county had made partial payments to Omnigo and is seeking a credit or refund
- Worst case scenario involves using any Omnigo credit for patrol-side services until depleted

## Procurement Card Request
A request was made for an additional procurement card for detention staff to handle travel expenses and emergency purchases. The request came after an incident during a jail conference where only one staff member had a card for hotel check-in. Commissioners expressed hesitation about issuing additional cards, referencing past issues. The matter was not formally decided during the meeting.

## Solid Waste Issue
Brief discussion indicated that a solid waste measure did not pass, described as a "reprieve for the moment" rather than a permanent solution.

## Additional Administrative Items
- Bills were reviewed and approved for payment
- Discussion about invoices that had been incorrectly sent to a museum instead of the commission office for approximately one year
- Commissioners planned a walkthrough of the courthouse to inspect facilities
- Camera installation was mentioned as an upcoming project
- The commission noted that the governor voted against a special legislative session to address gas tax concerns

The meeting concluded with commissioners planning to conduct a courthouse walkthrough and staff noting they had no remaining discretionary funds for the current period.
shortSummary:
This summary captures the key updates from the county commission meeting:

The commission addressed a recent state auditor's report revealing that 17 of 18 closed sessions included unauthorized discussions. Commissioners acknowledged the findings, noting they lack dedicated legal counsel, but affirmed their ongoing efforts to strictly comply with Sunshine Law recommendations. 

The board approved the previous meeting minutes and accepted a janitorial services bid from Mike Kenney. Under new business, the sheriff's department secured approval to switch to Cadence Software for jail management due to ongoing issues with their current vendor, Omnigo. Finally, the commission reviewed the $4,300 annual insurance cost for the old jail and discussed options for potentially selling the property.
